title: Franciscans today
hookLine: friars in cities, soup kitchens and missions

cards: Before sunrise in a big city, a line is already forming outside a side door: men with backpacks, a mother with a stroller, an old man in a coat too heavy for the weather.

The door opens, and the person holding it is a friar. Down the street, another hears confessions in a downtown church at lunchtime. Across an ocean, another teaches in a village school, or sits with the sick in a clinic.
Francis died on the bare ground in Assisi. His brothers never stopped walking. Today, where you might find them now.

teach.h: NOT A HILLTOP, BUT THE ROAD.
teach.b: Francis didn't found a monastery on a hilltop. He sent his brothers out. His Rule pictures them going through the world owning nothing, working with their hands, taking what they need as poor men do.
So the friars ended up where people are, in towns, then cities, and that's still the shape.

The family of Francis now has several branches of friars, among them the Friars Minor, the Conventuals, and the Capuchins from a few days ago. There are the Poor Clares behind their grilles, praying for the world.
There are Franciscan sisters running schools and hospitals. And there are lay Franciscans, married people with jobs and kids, who follow Francis in ordinary life. What do they do?
Ordinary things, close to the poor: a soup kitchen, a shelter, a parish on a block nobody else wanted, a chaplain in a prison or hospital, a mission far from home.

Jesus's words in Matthew could hang over the door, in the Douay-Rheims: "For I was hungry, and you gave me to eat; I was thirsty, and you gave me to drink; I was a stranger, and you took me in." One more thing.
Francis is often said to have told people to preach the Gospel always and use words only if necessary. The early sources don't record him saying it.
What his early Rule does say is close: all the brothers should preach by their deeds.

teach.h: I WAS A STRANGER, AND YOU TOOK ME IN.
teach.b: The friar at that side door is doing just that.

how: Franciscan friars and sisters serve in parishes, soup kitchens, shelters, schools, hospitals and missions, and Catholics often support their works with gifts of money, food or time.

games.why: his Rule pictures the brothers going through the world, poor and working. so the friars ended up where people are, and they still do.

practice: Bring to mind one place near you that feeds people, shelters them or sits with them when they're sick, run by friars or sisters or someone else entirely, and picture its door and the line outside it.
Choose one small gift you could give, a few dollars, a bag of groceries, an hour, or simply finding out where it is; if you pray, pray for the people in that line and the people holding the door.

wordCard.voice: Franciscans today. Friars, sisters, Poor Clares and lay followers of Francis, still close to the poor, in cities, kitchens and missions. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: the Order of Friars Minor, the lesser brothers. it's why friars sign their names with OFM.

carryVoice: Your line: still walking. Preaching by deeds, the way his early Rule asked. One thousand two hundred twenty-seven days now.
